title: Goldman Sachs upgrades global equities to overweight, favoring U.S. and Asia - TradingView
text: Goldman Sachs upgrades global equities to overweight, favoring U.S. and Asia Less than 1 min read GS ACWI Goldman Sachs Group has upgraded its three-month outlook on global equities to overweight from neutral, citing strong earnings prospects and improved valuations after a recent market rally stalled. Strategists led by Christian Mueller-Glissmann said earnings growth continues to support stocks, while a pullback driven by higher oil prices and bond yields has made valuations more attractive ahead of the Q3 earnings season, according to Bloomberg . "Earnings growth remains supportive for equities and the recent valuation de-rating has improved asymmetry into the third-quarter earnings season," Mueller-Glissmann said. The team remains overweight on U.S. and Asian equities and underweight on European stocks. Goldman favors a barbell strategy combining global technology stocks with selective rate-sensitive, bond-proxy equities. Higher interest rates and energy prices remain the main near-term risks, while uncertainty surrounding U.S. midterm elections could add to market volatility. Goldman maintains an overweight stance on equities over 12 months, matching its upgraded three-month outlook. The strategists remain neutral on bonds over three months but favor them over a 12-month horizon.
